prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: a single fine-line architectural illustration for the Chinese heritage collection 访古.
Image 1 is the STYLE MASTER, an existing Vairocana Buddha contour drawing. Match its elegant, delicate, slightly organic thin lines, restrained detail, generous blank areas, and consistent visual density. Image 2 (and subsequent photos if applicable) is SUBJECT GEOMETRY ONLY: draw the actual named monument in that reference, preserving its identifying silhouette, roof type, visible storey count, bay count, openings, and proportions.
Create a refined, sparse BLACK INK ON PURE WHITE line drawing. Use confident fine contours with a few finer internal structural lines. All surfaces remain WHITE; use outlines for doors and windows rather than dark fills. No solid shadows, no broad grey shading, no crosshatching, no pencil grain, no texture, no gradient. No color, no gold, no black background. The white will become transparent and the ink the relevant dynasty color in the website.
Show the complete monument, centered, approximately straight-on at facade level, with verticals vertical and minimal perspective. Use only a few short ground lines. Remove tourists, foliage, vehicles, wires, modern signage, fences obstructing the structure, neighboring distractions and sky. Preserve architectural ornament selectively, without filling every roof tile or brick. No invented features. No labels, letters, calligraphy, dimension lines, captions, watermark, frame or border.
Wide compositions: landscape 1536×1024, entire building occupies about 82% of canvas width, roof/apex and base uncut, balanced breathing room. Tall pagodas: portrait 1024×1536, entire pagoda occupies about 82% of height, centred with equal side margins, apex and base uncut.


Subject: Guanyin Pavilion at Dule Temple, Jizhou, Tianjin, China (天津独乐寺观音阁), extant Liao building of984. Image1 is ONLY the line STYLE master; Images2 and3 are two ACTUAL frontal photographs of this one pavilion. Preserve the very distinctive wide rectangular TWO EXTERIOR STOREY pavilion with an intermediate hidden storey, exactly TWO tiled eave roofs plus ONE projecting open balcony floor between them. The balcony floor is a flat cantilevered wood platform with railings and large exposed supporting dougong BELOW; it is NOT a third roof. The upper main roof is hip-and-gable, deeply projecting with gently upturned corners; from the photographed almost straight frontal facade-level position the front roof plane is strongly foreshortened. Follow the actual photo profile rather than inventing a tall triangular pagoda peak. Lower eaves are a shallower tiled skirt around the ground floor. There are FIVE front bays, the center three occupied by framed door/window openings and the two outer end bays mostly solid walls, on BOTH storeys. Upper facade has three open rectangular double-shutter windows behind a long continuous open balcony railing; keep these openings as WHITE outlines. The ground facade has three framed double-door openings. Retain large spaced Liao dougong clusters beneath the two eaves and the balcony floor, but simplify their internal detail. Preserve long slender red-in-photo corner support props from the lower roof to the upper eaves and from the platform to the lower eaves, using single slim double-line outlines. Retain only silhouettes of the two plaque boards, one centered above ground doors and one upper center, completely blank. Preserve the low stone plinth and short broad steps. Remove the giant incense burner, lamps, tree in front of the left center door, foliage, trunks, fencing, visitors, all signs, all writing, adjacent halls and courtyard clutter. Draw only this complete pavilion, centered, width around80percent of landscape1536x1024canvas, ample white margins on all sides, eaves uncropped. White walls, windows, doors and roof surfaces. Do not fill dark window holes. Only selective roof rib indications, no tile grid, no dense engraving or hatching. Fine sparse gently organic black contours, visual density matching Buddha master.

site_recommendation.name: 独乐寺
site_recommendation.lede: 蓟州老城里，观音阁以两重深檐和一道平座舒展立面。阁内暗层把梁柱连接在一起，楼阁的空间围绕高大的观音像展开。
facts: 现存观音阁重建于辽统和二年（984），与山门共同保存辽代木构形制。
观音阁面阔五间、进深四间，外观两层，内部含暗层共三层。
上层设内外平座回廊，梁枋和斗拱将两圈立柱联结成整体。

verification: 已查看母版、两张输入与原始生成；五开间、两重瓦檐、一道平座及三门三窗的主体轮廓成立；树、香炉、人员与文字已去除，四边无裁切。
